entries: Abjurer archmages create powerful magical wards. Their magic allows them to quarantine dangerous foes, and they're adept at nullifying the spells of even fellow archmages. Despite their focus on protective magic, abjurer archmages are formidable offensive combatants.

Although all archmages have mastered incredible magical power, some specialize in a particular school of magic, pushing their abilities to greater heights in that area. These archmages stock their spellbooks with spells from their preferred school and have developed unique magical techniques.
Immense and specialized magical prowess isn't an end in its own right. It's how one uses their power that matters.

images.title: Archmages from Each School of Magic: 1. Conjurer 2. Abjurer 3. Necromancer 4. Illusionist 5. Diviner 6. Enchanter 7. Transmuter 8. Evoker

entries: {@creature Baelnorn|AU|Baelnorns} are deathless guardians of treasures and lore. Each baelnorn was once a living person who undertook a non-evil process to preserve their existence that involved either a divine blessing or an ancient ritual. Many baelnorns were once elves. In fact, ancient elves were the first to discover the secret to becoming a baelnorn.

{@creature Baelnorn|AU|Baelnorns} typically dedicate themselves to protecting vaults, castles, or ruins. In the Forgotten Realms, elf baelnorns protect the site of Myth Drannor, a ruined ancient city that was once a magical metropolis. Many enjoy studying ancient lore lost to living scholars. As only the most dedicated can endure the transition into a baelnorn, baelnorns are often proud of the eternal life they've achieved.

Unlike liches, baelnorns almost never have soul jars, although some baelnorns associated with a holy site might house their souls within a sacred relic. Many baelnorns create magical clones their spirits can inhabit if their bodies are destroyed.

Newly risen baelnorns look much as they did in life, albeit with glowing white eyes. They often continue their prior roles as guardians, sages, or teachers. A baelnorn's hair and flesh gradually fade away over many years; the oldest resemble stately skeletons in diaphanous raiment.

{@creature Baelnorn|AU|Baelnorns} spend years poring over arcane tomes to aid their transition into undeath, and even those who weren't mages at the time of their transformation typically spend much of their long existences studying magical lore. As a result, baelnorns can cast powerful spells.

entries.name: Baelnorn Lairs
entries: Most baelnorns guard sites of historical or spiritual importance, sometimes long past the time anyone living remembers the sites. A few baelnorns instead guard great secrets, artifacts, or significant family lines, usually within such ancient sites. A baelnorn's protected site might be a grove of supernatural trees, the ruined capitol of a long-lost nation, or a library holding eons-old magical lore.
A baelnorn extends its presence into the region it inhabits, creating the following effects:

items.name: Projection
entries: While in its lair, the baelnorn can cast {@spell Project Image|XPHB}, requiring no spell components and using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 19}). The spell's range is limited to the baelnorn's lair.

items.name: Travel Ward
entries: Creatures can't use teleportation or planar travel to enter or exit the lair.
If the baelnorn is destroyed or moves its lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately.

Most baelnorns embody the ideal of scholarly focus and self-sacrifice for the benefit of society. If you meet one, I suspect they'd appreciate sharing a lively conversation or ten. Forever can be a lonely existence.

Physical distance is no concern to conjurer archmages. These archmages can teleport themselves and others across nations and planar boundaries in the blink of an eye. They create magical effects from thin air or pull them from other planes of existence.

{@creature Darkenbeast|AU|Darkenbeasts} are ferocious, bestial hunters created from ordinary animals by sinister spellcasters. Regardless of darkenbeasts' original forms, the magic used to create them twists them into fanged horrors with leathery wings. Most darkenbeasts have luminous bones that glow through their skin; they resemble eerie flying skeletons as they soar through the night sky. A darkenbeast is loyal to its creators, who can extract the magic used to transform it in a dramatic display that's fatal to the darkenbeast.

{@creature Darkenbeast|AU|Darkenbeasts} might have vestigial characteristics of the animals they were before transformation. Roll on or choose a result from the Darkenbeast Origin table as inspiration for these cosmetic features.

rows: Cobra, so it has a flared neck and scaly skin.
Fox, giving it reddish fur and vulpine features.
{@creature Panther|XMM}, so it has sharp claws and a high-pitched scream.
Rabbit, giving it long ears and a skittish demeanor.
Turtle, giving it a blunt snout and shell-like carapace.
{@creature Wolf|XMM}, so it emits eerie howls.
entries.caption: Darkenbeast Origin

entries: Diviner archmages spy on distant lands and peer into the future. These archmages often anticipate others' actions and react seconds before events occur.
Enchanter archmages enjoy shaping minds. These archmages tinker with memories and compel others to follow their commands, either subtly or blatantly.
Evoker archmages wield unbridled destructive magic with surgical precision. They can carve out safe areas in an explosive blast, shielding themselves and allies while obliterating foes.

Created to be brute troops, groundling grunts love tearing flesh with their claws. If not controlled by a commanding leader, they're likely to slip away and pursue mayhem or to stop during a battle to feast on their kills.

A groundling that learns subtlety and self-control becomes an efficient killer. These groundling slayers are often entrusted with solo missions of stealth or assassination or are assigned to keep fractious groundlings in line. Slayers usually wait until after a fight is over before consuming foes they've slain.

Groundling stalkers enjoy ambushing and murdering foes from afar with their crossbows. Stalkers rarely maintain the element of surprise for long, as they roar in bloodthirsty delight when they strike.

Groundlings are hairy, stinky bullies and insatiable carnivores. They use their claws not only to disembowel their victims but also to dig traps, tunnel beneath buildings, and excavate hiding spots from which to ambush prey.

Groundlings are created, not born. Most are magical mutations of fierce burrowing animals. Groundlings often serve as shock troops or assassins for their creators, though leaderless groundlings sometimes pursue lives as killers or mercenaries.
Groundlings are victims of heinous magic. The brutality of evil never ends, and thus we must continue to fight against it.

images.title: From Left to Right: {@creature Groundling Slayer|AU}, {@creature Groundling Grunt|AU}, {@creature Groundling Stalker|AU}

entries: Illusionist archmages have mastered the tactile elements of illusory magic. They can create complex effects that seem vibrantly real and modify the subtlest details of illusory disguises, objects, and terrain.
Accompanied by blasts of frigid wind, a living cone of cold seeks sources of heat—such as living creatures—to freeze solid.

Magical energies unleashed during cataclysmic battles or catastrophic experiments can cause spell effects to come to life as living spells. These beings' magical energy is persistent, and they bear features resembling those of their origin spells—usually Conjuration or Evocation spells. Living spells typically linger in the region of their creation, subsisting on ambient magical energy and lashing out at creatures they encounter.

entries.name: Creating Living Spells
entries: Living spells come in many varieties; the stat blocks here are three examples. To make a living spell from a different spell, choose a damage-dealing Conjuration or Evocation spell of level 1–5 from the Wizard spell list. Then consult the Living Spell Customization table to see which stat block to customize based on the chosen spell's level.
Now make the following changes to the stat block:

items.name: Damage Immunity
items.entry: Replace the living spell's damage {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} with {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to the type (or types) of damage dealt by the chosen spell.

items.name: Magical Strike
items.entry: Change the damage type dealt by Magical Strike to one of the damage types dealt by the chosen spell.

items.name: Spell Mimicry
items.entry: Replace the effect of Spell Mimicry with the effect of the chosen spell. If that spell requires a saving throw, use the spell save DC from Spell Mimicry. If the spell involves an attack roll, use the attack bonus from the living spell's Magical Strike.

entries: For example, if you turn {@spell Fireball|XPHB} (a level 3 spell) into a living spell, customize the {@creature Living Vitriolic Sphere|AU} stat block. The living fireball has {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Fire damage instead of Acid damage, deals Fire damage with its Magical Strike, and replicates {@i Fireball} with Spell Mimicry.
A living thunderwave roars and rumbles, booming with thunder like an unnatural storm cloud.
A living vitriolic sphere is a perpetually roiling, fuming miasma. It scars the ground beneath itself with dribbles of acid.
Necromancer archmages use necrotic magic to siphon life from their enemies and empower the undead. Many necromancers think nothing of raising the dead and sending them into battle.

{@creature Spellguard|AU|Spellguards} are professional bodyguards who specialize in repelling magical aggression. {@creature Spellguard|AU|Spellguards} supplement their imposing armor with magical defenses to protect themselves and their charges. They most often work for spellcasters distrustful of rivals, but a spellguard might guard anyone who fears magical foes. The {@item Spellguard Shield|XDMG} is named after this tradition, as that item's power replicates a spellguard's protections.
Silverymoon's spellguards have my undying loyalty and gratitude. I trust them with my life.

The most gifted mortal mages can sometimes peer beyond reality to glimpse pure, untrammeled magic. Directly accessing this energy requires years of careful study and dangerous rituals. Any mage who succeeds taps into esoteric powers that strip away the mage's physical body, blending their mortal mind with raw magic to form a quasi-corporeal entity called a taisus, or an ascended mage.

A taisus initially retains the personality and values of the mortal mage it was before, but its mindset eventually becomes alien, taking on a long-term outlook that seems callous to mortals. Most taisuses seek to draw energies from places of significant magical power, such as planar portals or quintessence pools, in order to create bizarre magic items, reshape the nature of magic, or lead others to duplicate their eldritch ascension. A taisus's end goal is unfathomable to mortal minds.
Transmuter archmages transform themselves or their surroundings. These archmages manipulate combatants to suit their own whims.
{@i Corrupted Force of Evil}

An immortal mage and Fiend with an implacable hatred for {@book Tiamat|XDMG|8|Tiamat}, {@creature Venger|AU} seeks to rule nations by amassing sycophants and long-lost magical artifacts. Though his bat-like wings allow him to fly, {@creature Venger|AU} prefers to ride on his trusted flying steed, a {@creature Nightmare|XMM} that lurks on the Ethereal Plane until it's needed. {@creature Venger|AU} sends his adviser, {@creature Shadow Demon|XMM}, to survey distant lands, then weaves interlocking plans based on Shadow Demon's reports.

{@creature Venger|AU} was once a good-hearted human studying wizardry under the cryptic tutelage of his father. In time, {@creature Venger|AU} grew impatient and sought to increase his magical prowess by dabbling in minor pacts with demons. He eventually met demons who worshipped {@book Tharizdun|XDMG|8|Tharizdun} the Chained God, an entity the demons believed powerful enough to create whole planes of existence. {@creature Venger|AU} yearned to forge a pact with this entity, believing that doing so would give him immense power.

With the help of these Tharizdun-worshipping demons, {@creature Venger|AU} opened a brief window into the demiplane of Tharizdun's imprisonment. The demons had neglected to mention that the souls of all who look on the Chained God face certain doom. As {@creature Venger|AU} gazed on this entity—an unknowable, indescribable blend of demonic and aberrant influence—Venger's form warped, and the last traces of goodness sloughed off him. The demons collected this good essence and locked it in a vault that they spirited away to a distant corner of the Material Plane. {@creature Venger|AU} emerged from this encounter as a cruel, twisted version of himself, exalted now with immortality and magical might, and he vowed to free the Chained God.

At first, {@creature Venger|AU} earnestly pursued this promise. In time, though, he grew to despise his vow and neglected it in favor of his own pursuit of power. Now he no longer wants Tharizdun freed, knowing his disloyalty could make him a target of Tharizdun's wrath.

After abandoning his quest to free Tharizdun, {@creature Venger|AU} sought to use several {@item Orb of Dragonkind|XDMG|Orbs of Dragonkind} to control Tiamat. This futile endeavor earned Venger Tiamat's lifelong enmity. {@creature Venger|AU} now plots endlessly to destroy or subjugate Tiamat, among other nefarious designs. Roll on or choose a result from the Venger's Schemes table to inspire Venger's next power play.

rows: Imprison those who would oppose him in a vast labyrinth of his own creation called the Maze of Darkness.
Summon a two-headed, Abyssal dragon called the {@creature Demodragon|WttHC} (use the {@creature Adult Black Dragon|XMM} stat block) and unleash it on a nation.
Recruit heroes to help him thwart the League of Malevolence, a villainous group led by his former lackey, the mage Kelek.
Disguise himself as a wise wizard or noble paladin to trick innocents into giving him a powerful artifact.
Assemble six powerful magic items and use their magic at a site called the Hall of Bones to gain enough power to destroy Tiamat for good.
Find an artifact called the Box of Balefire and keep it away from other villains; {@creature Venger|AU} fears it could unleash Tharizdun.
entries.caption: Venger's Schemes

entries.name: Venger's Lairs
entries: {@creature Venger|AU} keeps several lairs in each of the worlds he visits. Each is a castle perched above or extending from the side of a treacherous cliff, but none are identical.
Venger's presence fouls the regions his lairs inhabit, creating the following effects:

items.name: Desolate Terrain
entries: Plant life within 1 mile of a lair withers and dies, creating a barren wasteland of cracked dirt.

items.name: Tormented Rest
entries: Abyssal whispers plague visitors' dreams. Whenever a creature other than {@creature Venger|AU} or his allies finishes a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} within 1 mile of a lair, it must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw or gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level.
If Venger dies or moves a lair elsewhere, these effects end immediately.
